headline: Right to Repair Law Takes Effect as Green Claims Proposal Scrapped
summary: The EU Right to Repair directive has taken effect, imposing mandatory repair obligations on consumer goods alongside a new Commission consultation on repairability. Meanwhile, reports indicate the European Commission plans to abandon the proposed Green Claims Directive.

items.title: EU Right to Repair Directive Enters into Force
items.what: The EU Right to Repair directive has taken effect, establishing mandatory repair obligations. Concurrently, the European Commission opened a public consultation seeking feedback on further repairability standards for products.
items.meaning: Directly impacts your power tools and garden equipment portfolio, requiring accessible spare parts, technical information, and product designs that facilitate consumer repair.
items.action: Assess tool design, battery accessibility, and spare parts availability against repair requirements.

sources.title: New Law on Right to Repair Takes Effect

items.title: European Commission Reportedly Drops Green Claims Directive
items.what: Reports indicate the European Commission intends to withdraw the proposed Green Claims Directive, dropping plans for mandatory ex-ante independent verification of environmental claims.
items.meaning: This proposal is reported as scrapped and is not law. If confirmed, strict pre-approval requirements for environmental marketing of your tools and battery platform will not apply.
items.action: Maintain robust substantiation for sustainability claims under existing consumer protection rules.
